items.prompt: Black to move. Before you play, list White's checks and threats. What is White threatening? (Name the move.)

claims.statement: If Black passes, Rd8 is checkmate.

hints: Start with White's checks. The rook is the only piece that can give one.
Which square on the back rank would the rook check from?
The rook goes to the far end of the d-file.
items.explain: Black's king has no flight square behind the pawns and nothing can block or take on d8, so Rd8 would be checkmate if Black passed.

items.prompt: White to move. List the captures first. Which capture wins a piece?

claims.statement: Rxd5 wins the knight and keeps the material.
Rxd5 is the engine's best move.

hints: Count what White can capture. There is one capture.
Is the target defended by anything?
items.explain: The knight on d5 is attacked by the rook and no black piece defends it, so the capture wins it.

feedback_by_move.d2d7: Rd7 gives up the rook's grip on the knight and wins nothing.

items.prompt: White to move. Look at the checks. Which check also wins material?

claims.statement: Nc7+ wins the rook for the cost of at most the knight.
Nc7+ is the engine's best move.

hints: List every check White has. Which one lands on a square that attacks something else?
The checking piece should attack the king and another piece at once.
The knight jumps to the c-file.
items.explain: The knight on c7 checks the king and attacks the rook on a8, so the king must move and the rook falls.

items.prompt: White to move. Qxd5 captures a pawn. Predict, then check: does it win material?

claims.statement: Qxd5 loses at least four pawns of value compared with the best move.

hints: Count the attackers on d5 and the defenders of d5.
One attacker against one defender: who ends up capturing last?
After Qxd5, can Black take the queen?
items.explain: White attacks d5 once and Black defends it once, so the queen is lost for a pawn after Qxd5 Qxd5.

items.prompt: White to move, nothing labeled. List the checks and captures for both sides. Does a forcing move help?

claims.statement: No line wins more than a pawn for White.
The engine sees the position as roughly level.

hints: Write down every check White has, then every capture.
Do any of those captures win something after the recapture?
Both sides are fully developed; the tension is only in the centre.
items.explain: Every capture is answered by a recapture of equal value and there are no useful checks, so the right plan is a quiet move.

items.prompt: White to move. Rxd5 takes a pawn. Predict, then check: what can Black answer with first?

claims.statement: Rxd5 is far worse than the best move.

hints: Look at Black's checks after Rxd5, not only at White's gain.
Which white piece is left without a defender?
The black rook can take on e1 with check.
items.explain: After Rxd5 the rook on e1 loses its defender, and Black's capture on e1 is check and mate; the rook capture on e8 was mate for White.
